entities.summary: Do Ho Suh is a South Korean artist who works primarily in sculpture, installation, and drawing. Suh is well known for re-creating architectural structures and objects using fabric in what the artist describes as an "act of memorialization." After earning a Bachelor of Fine Arts and Master of Fine Arts from Seoul National University in Korean painting, Suh began experimenting with sculpture and installation while studying at the Rhode Island School of Design (RISD). He graduated with a Bachelor of Fine Arts in painting from RISD in 1994, and went on to Yale where he graduated with a Master of Fine Arts in sculpture in 1997.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Do Ho Suh's work in re-creating architectural structures and objects using fabric has contributed to a growing interest in sustainable art practices and memorialization through creative means. His use of fabric as a medium also highlights the potential for repurposing and upcycling materials.
